session_identity.applies_to: every scan request, general and specialized alike
why: session_id is the key multi-turn correlation groups a caller's turns by.
Without it the stateful layer has nothing to correlate.
agent_id is what scope enforcement attributes an action to. Without it,
a declared scope cannot be matched to the agent performing the action.
source_application identifies the SDK for support and telemetry.
An SDK omitting these does not fail loudly. It silently receives a
weaker product than the one the customer believes they installed.
The backend reads the API key from Authorization: Bearer or
X-Shrike-API-Key only. A request that carries the key in X-API-Key has
no recognized credential, resolves to the anonymous tier, and receives
anonymous-tier scanning with no error to say so.
The conversation history goes in conversation_history, NOT in context.
context is an object carrying the session identity. A string context is
accepted on the wire but carries no session_id or agent_id, so multi-turn
correlation has no key to group turns by and scope enforcement has no
agent to attribute the scan to. Nothing reports the loss.

file_path.note: ScanFile with no content argument resolves here.

file_content.note: ScanFile with a content argument resolves here. One method, two channels, decided by an argument: getting it backwards scans a file body against path-traversal rules.

rag_context.note: Multiple chunks serialize as a JSON array so the backend can split them apart again. A naive join merges two documents and loses the boundary an injection usually sits on.

why: Not a specialized content type: its own route and its own detector.
Routing it through the specialized endpoint would scan the tool
description as opaque text and miss tool poisoning entirely.
